rows.content:
# Penthouses and Roof Structures

---

## Learning Goal

After reading this article, you should be able to:

Determine when a penthouse or roof structure is exempt from height and FAR calculations under PD 1096 Rule VII; identify the three conditions for penthouse exemption (occupancy, area ≤ 1/3 roof area, and height); distinguish roof structures (tanks, towers, mechanical) from habitable penthouses for code compliance purposes.

## Module Header

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| **Module Focus** | Penthouse Height and Area Limits, Prohibited Uses, Towers & Spires, Skylight Glass Rules, Balcony Railing Requirements |
| **Legal Basis (PH)** | PD 1096, Rule XII, Sections 1208–1210 |
| **IBC Counterpart** | IBC Section 1511 (Penthouses), Section 2405 (Sloped Glazing and Skylights) |
| **LEA Area** | Area 3 — Architectural Design & Site Planning (40% of exam weight) |
| **Difficulty** | Advanced |
| **Spaced Repetition** | Review on Day 1, Day 3, Day 7, and Day 14 |

---

## Hook Scenario

The developer calls you at 7 PM, excited: they want to convert the mechanical penthouse of their newly completed 24-storey BGC tower into a rooftop bar and event venue. The penthouse is 35% of the roof area and stands 5.40 meters above the roof deck. You recognize three immediate problems before the conversation is over.

First, the penthouse area at 35% already exceeds the **1/3 (33.3%) aggregate area limit** of Sec. 1210.b — it should have been caught during design. Second, the 5.40-meter height is above the **3.60-meter limit** for non-elevator/non-tank penthouses under Sec. 1210.a, though 8.40 meters is allowed for elevator and tank enclosures. Third — and most critically — converting the penthouse to a bar and event venue violates Sec. 1210.c: penthouses are prohibited from use for any purpose other than sheltering mechanical equipment or shaft openings. The moment the penthouse is used for habitable purposes, it is **reclassified as an additional storey** — restarting every building height, fire-rating, and egress calculation for the entire building.

This article is the definitive guide to penthouses, skylights, and the architectural elements that straddle the boundary between roof and habitable space — where one wrong design decision cascades through BHL calculations, GFA exclusions, and occupancy classifications.

---

## Core Concepts

### Concept 1: Penthouse Height Limits — Two Tiers (Sec. 1210.a)

PD 1096 establishes two distinct height limits for penthouses measured **above the roof level**:

**Tier 1 — Elevator Machine Rooms and Water Tanks (Non-Type V Construction):**
- Maximum height: **8.40 m** above the roof.
- Applies to: tank enclosures (water storage, fire reserve tanks) and elevator machine rooms, on buildings that are not Type V construction.
- rationale: elevator overrun clearance and tank capacities require greater headroom that cannot be accommodated within the 3.60 m general limit.

**Tier 2 — All Other Penthouses:**
- Maximum height: **3.60 m** above the roof.
- Applies to: stairway enclosures, mechanical equipment rooms (other than elevator machinery), generator rooms, cooling tower enclosures.
- rationale: standard mechanical headroom is achievable within 3.60 m; exceeding this implies the structure is being used as a habitable space (triggering the "additional storey" conversion).

Board exam trap: when a question asks about penthouse height "in all cases," there is no single answer — always identify whether it is for elevator/tank or general use.

### Concept 2: Aggregate Area Limit — 1/3 of the Roof (Sec. 1210.b)

The total aggregate footprint of **all** penthouses and roof structures combined must not exceed **1/3 of the area of the supporting roof below**. This is a collective limit — not per-structure.

- If a roof is 900 sq.m, the maximum total penthouse footprint is **300 sq.m**.
- Multiple smaller penthouses (elevator room + staircase enclosure + tank room) all count toward the 1/3 aggregate.
- This limit prevents penthouses from collectively becoming an additional floor under a nominally different name.

**BHL Interaction**: Penthouses that comply with Sec. 1210 requirements (correct height, correct area, correct use) are **excluded from Building Height Limit (BHL) calculations** under NBCP Rule VIII. They sit above the regulated building height as permitted roof projections. However, if a penthouse violates the prohibited-use rule (Sec. 1210.c), it is reclassified as an additional storey and **counted toward BHL** — potentially making the building non-compliant with the zoning height restriction.

### Concept 3: Prohibited Uses — The Additional Storey Trigger (Sec. 1210.c)

This is the most legally consequential provision in Sec. 1210. Penthouses may be used **only** for:
1. Shelter of mechanical equipment (HVAC, elevators, generators, water tanks).
2. Enclosure of vertical shaft openings (stairwells, elevator shafts).

Prohibited uses include:
- Residential occupancy (apartments, staff quarters).
- Commercial use (restaurants, offices, event venues).
- Any habitable space.

**Consequence of Prohibited Use**: The penthouse is legally treated as an **additional storey** of the building. This has cascading effects:
- Building height recalculation for BHL compliance.
- Additional storey count for fire-rating purposes (Type of Construction adequacy).
- Additional egress requirements (minimum stairwells, travel distances).
- Re-computation of **Gross Floor Area (GFA)** — the converted penthouse floor area is added to the GFA, affecting Floor Area Ratio (FAR) compliance.

**GFA Interaction for Balconies**: In contrast, **balconies** are excluded from GFA calculations when the balcony depth does not exceed **1.50 m** (per NBCP IRR and most zoning ordinances) or where the total balcony area per floor does not exceed a threshold (typically interpreted as balconies ≤ 10 sq.m aggregate per floor per unit are excluded). Balconies exceeding these thresholds are included in GFA, reducing the building's development capacity.

### Concept 4: Skylight Glass Requirements (Sec. 1208)

Skylights present a serious public safety risk — falling glass from overhead skylights can be lethal. Sec. 1208 establishes a hierarchy of glass types and support requirements:

**General Rule — Wired Glass Required:**
All skylights shall use **wired glass** except in specific exempted conditions (Sec. 1208).

**Flat Wired Glass:**
- Maximum span between supports: **625 mm**.
- Use: standard skylight panels over occupied spaces.

**Corrugated Wired Glass:**
- Maximum span between supports: **1.50 m**.
- The corrugation provides additional structural stiffness, justifying the longer span.

**Exemptions from Wired Glass:**
1. **Skylights over vertical shafts** (2+ storeys): plain (non-wired) glass is permitted if the shaft is ventilated with a net free area of at least **1/8 of the shaft's cross-sectional area** (minimum ventilation opening: **1.20 m**).
2. **Non-wired glass with protective screens above and below**: wire screens with wire diameter ≥ 2.5 mm and mesh openings ≤ 25 mm must be installed on both sides of the glass.
3. **Photographer's skylights**: metal frames with plate glass (no wire netting) are permitted — the controlled studio environment removes the public-safety concern.
4. **Greenhouse skylights**: ordinary glass is permitted when the greenhouse is **≤ 6.00 m above grade** — the low height limits fall-impact risk.
5. **Glass in floors/sidewalks**: must be supported by metal or reinforced concrete frames; glass minimum **12.5 mm thick**.
6. **Groups A and J buildings**: metal frames are not required for skylight framing (these are typically low-rise residential and miscellaneous structures).

### Concept 5: Towers, Spires, and the Frontage/Base Rules (Sec. 1210.e)

Architectural towers and spires — clock towers, bell towers, decorative campaniles, communication masts, and neon sign structures — are permitted on rooftops subject to strict dimensional controls:

1. **Street frontage limit**: The base width of any tower or spire must not exceed **1/4 of the street frontage** of the building.
2. **Base area limit**: The base footprint of the tower must not exceed **150 sq.m** unless the tower itself conforms to the Type of Construction requirements for the entire building.
3. **Cross-section rule**: If the tower's cross-sectional area **exceeds 10.00 sq.m** at any point above the roof, its **supporting structural frame must extend down to the ground** (not just to the roof level).
4. **Skeleton towers** (radio masts, neon sign frames): permitted on rooftops without the base area restriction when the structure is an open skeleton frame.
5. **Balcony railing height**: Exterior balconies, landings, and porches **more than 750 mm above grade** must have railings of **incombustible materials** (Sec. 1209). The railing height itself must comply with Rule VIII setback provisions and the NSCP (typically minimum 1.05 m for balconies in residential occupancies).

---

## PH vs. USA Comparative Analysis

| Topic | PH — PD 1096 (Rule XII, Sec. 1208–1210) | USA — IBC (Sec. 1511, Sec. 2405) |
|---|---|---|
| **Penthouse height — elevator/tank** | Max 8.40 m above roof (non-Type V) | IBC Sec. 1511.2: Max 18 ft (5.49 m) above roof for elevator enclosures |
| **Penthouse height — general** | Max 3.60 m above roof | IBC Sec. 1511.2: Max 12 ft (3.66 m) above roof (similar, slight variation) |
| **Aggregate penthouse area** | ≤ 1/3 of supporting roof area | IBC Sec. 1511.2: ≤ 1/3 of supporting roof area (identical) |
| **Prohibited uses** | Cannot be used for occupancy; triggers additional storey | IBC Sec. 1511.1: Penthouses are unoccupied — violation reclassifies as additional story |
| **BHL exclusion** | Excluded from BHL if code-compliant | IBC: Not counted in building height if meets 1511 requirements |
| **Skylight glazing standard** | Wired glass required (flat: 625mm, corrugated: 1.50m spans) | IBC Sec. 2405.3: Sloped glazing — laminated glass, tempered glass, or wired glass with thickness and span tables |
| **Skylight over shaft** | Plain glass allowed with 1/8 cross-section ventilation (min 1.20m) | IBC Sec. 2405.4: Skylights over shafts allowed with specific glazing types and area limitations |
| **Glass in floors** | Metal/RC frame; ≥ 12.5 mm thick glass | IBC Sec. 2409: Floor and sidewalk lights — safety glass ≥ 6.4 mm or approved assemblies |
| **Greenhouse skylight** | Ordinary glass if ≤ 6.00 m above grade | IBC Sec. 2405.5: Greenhouses — plastic or glass permitted; height-based risk assessment |
| **Tower frontage limit** | ≤ 1/4 of street frontage | IBC: No universal frontage fraction; local zoning governs |
| **Tower base area** | ≤ 150 sq.m unless building-type compliant | IBC: No specific base area limit; governed by structural adequacy per ASCE 7 |
| **Cross-section structure rule** | If > 10.00 sq.m cross-section → frame to ground | IBC: Structural continuity required per ASCE 7; no specific cross-section threshold |
| **Balcony railing material** | Incombustible if balcony > 750 mm above grade | IBC Sec. 1015: Guards required ≥ 30 in. (762 mm); material not restricted to incombustible |
| **Balcony GFA exclusion** | Balconies ≤ 10 sq.m typically excluded from GFA | IBC: No GFA concept; governed by local zoning ordinances |

**Key Philosophical Difference**: The Philippine code's penthouse provisions are embedded in a regulatory ecosystem that includes BHL, GFA, and FAR — meaning penthouse design decisions directly affect the building's maximum development capacity under zoning law. The IBC's penthouse provisions (Sec. 1511) are standalone construction requirements focused on structural and fire safety, with zoning implications handled separately by local ordinances. Philippine architects must simultaneously check Sec. 1210 against the zoning resolution's BHL and FAR tables, something the IBC framework does not require in a single integrated review.

---

## Hard Data / Cheat Sheet Table

| Parameter | Value | Code Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Max penthouse height (elevator/tank, non-Type V) | 8.40 m above roof | Sec. 1210.a |
| Max penthouse height (all other cases) | 3.60 m above roof | Sec. 1210.a |
| Aggregate penthouse area limit | ≤ 1/3 of supporting roof area | Sec. 1210.b |
| Penthouse prohibited use consequence | Treated as additional storey | Sec. 1210.c |
| Tower/spire max base area | ≤ 150 sq.m (unless building-type compliant) | Sec. 1210.e |
| Tower/spire max street frontage | ≤ 1/4 of street frontage | Sec. 1210.e |
| Tower cross-section triggering ground frame | > 10.00 sq.m at any point | Sec. 1210.e |
| Flat wired glass max span | 625 mm between supports | Sec. 1208.b |
| Corrugated wired glass max span | 1.50 m between supports | Sec. 1208.b |
| Plain glass over shaft — ventilation min | 1/8 of shaft cross-section; min 1.20 m | Sec. 1208 |
| Non-wired glass screen wire diameter | ≥ 2.5 mm | Sec. 1208 |
| Non-wired glass screen mesh opening | ≤ 25 mm | Sec. 1208 |
| Greenhouse skylight (ordinary glass) | Only if ≤ 6.00 m above grade | Sec. 1208 |
| Glass in floors/sidewalks — min thickness | ≥ 12.5 mm | Sec. 1208 |
| Balcony railing material threshold | Incombustible if > 750 mm above grade | Sec. 1209 |
| Bay/oriel roof covering | Same material as main building roof | Sec. 1209 |
| Exterior balcony brackets (masonry wall) | Incombustible materials only | Sec. 1209 |
| Groups A and J — metal skylight frame | Not required | Sec. 1208.a |
| IBC penthouse height — elevator | Max 5.49 m (18 ft) | IBC Sec. 1511.2 |
| IBC penthouse height — general | Max 3.66 m (12 ft) | IBC Sec. 1511.2 |
| IBC aggregate penthouse area | ≤ 1/3 of roof area | IBC Sec. 1511.2 |

---

## Cross-Referencing

### BHL (Building Height Limit) Calculations — Rule VIII and Zoning Ordinances
Penthouse compliance with Sec. 1210 is prerequisite to the standard BHL exclusion recognized in Rule VIII and local zoning ordinances. A code-compliant penthouse sits **above** the BHL without being counted in the regulated height — it is treated as a permitted roof projection, similar to parapets, stair bulkheads, and mechanical equipment screens.

When a penthouse exceeds the height (8.40m or 3.60m), exceeds 1/3 of roof area, or is used for habitable purposes, it **loses the BHL exclusion**. The entire height of that penthouse is then added to the measured building height. In zones with tight height restrictions (e.g., height limit of 15m near airports or in heritage zones), a non-compliant penthouse can push a building above its permitted BHL — triggering building permit revocation proceedings.

### GFA Exclusions — Floor Area Ratio (FAR) Compliance
The GFA of penthouses complying with Sec. 1210 is typically excluded from the development's Total GFA for FAR computation. Once a penthouse is reclassified as an additional storey, its floor area is added to the GFA — which may cause the development to exceed the permissible FAR, requiring either redesign of the penthouse or reduction of another floor's area to compensate.

Similarly, balcony areas receive GFA exclusion treatment under most Philippine zoning ordinances — but this is conditional on balcony depth and aggregate area. Balconies with a projection exceeding the permitted exclusion threshold are included in GFA, directly affecting FAR compliance and potentially the number of sleaable or rentable units the building can contain.

### Rule VI — Type of Construction and Penthouse Wall Requirements
Sec. 1210.d ties penthouse construction requirements to the building's Type of Construction. For **Type III and Type IV** buildings: if the exterior walls or roof of the penthouse are at least 1.50 m from the property line, those penthouse elements need only be **1-hour fire-resistive and incombustible**. Walls ≤ 1.50 m from the exterior wall of a Type IV building must also meet the 1-hour fire-resistive incombustible standard. This is a proximity-based fire protection rule — penthouses close to property lines face higher spread-of-fire risk and therefore require fire-resistive construction.

### NSCP — Structural Requirements for Towers and Spires
The cross-section rule (>10 sq.m cross-section = frame to ground) in Sec. 1210.e is a structural stability requirement. Large towers generate substantial overturning moments from wind and seismic forces — these moments must be transferred through a continuous structural frame to the foundation, not just to the roof level. The NSCP governs the actual structural design of these frames, including seismic base shear distribution and foundation design for the additional lateral loads introduced by the tower.

---

## Active Learning Techniques

### Memory Aid — "8.4 and 3.6: Tanks Float High, Others Stay Low"
Penthouse height limits:
- **8.40 m** for elevator machinery and water **tanks** (they need more room to float their equipment higher).
- **3.60 m** for all other uses (standard mechanical headroom — "keep it low or it becomes a floor").

Associate 8.40 with the number 84 (8 stories × approx. 10.5 ft = a tower), and 3.60 with a single residential floor height — "if you can fit a bedroom in it, it's a storey."

### Memory Aid — "1/3 Roof, 1/4 Frontage, 1/8 Shaft" (The Fraction Rule)
Three critical fractions in this module:
- **1/3** of roof area → maximum aggregate penthouse footprint.
- **1/4** of street frontage → maximum tower/spire base width.
- **1/8** of shaft cross-section → minimum ventilation area for plain glass over shaft skylights (min 1.20m).

Say: *"One-third of the roof, one-quarter of the street, one-eighth of the shaft."*

### Memory Aid — "625 Flat, 1500 Corrugated" (Skylight Spans)
Flat wired glass: **625 mm** max span (about the width of a standard bathroom tile spacing).
Corrugated wired glass: **1,500 mm** (= **1.50 m**) max span.
The corrugation gives it 2.4× the flat glass span — the ribbing converts a weak flat plate into a structural shell.

### Memory Aid — "10 Square Meters: The Two Triggers"
The number **10.00 sq.m** appears twice in these sections — both in Article 20 and here:
- Article 20 (Sec. 1204): Max **single opening** in a 3-hour separation wall = **10.00 sq.m**.
- Article 21 (Sec. 1210.e): Tower cross-section **> 10.00 sq.m** → structural frame must extend to ground.

Both deal with a threshold of 10 sq.m — but in opposite contexts (opening size limit vs. structural trigger). Know which article each belongs to.

### If/Then Scenarios

**If** an architect places the elevator machine room penthouse at 9.00 m above the roof deck on a Type III building…
**Then** this violates Sec. 1210.a — the maximum for elevator/tank penthouses is **8.40 m**. The excess 0.60 m causes the penthouse to be treated as an additional storey.

**If** a developer wants to use a code-compliant penthouse as a co-working space for building tenants…
**Then** this violates Sec. 1210.c — penthouses may only shelter mechanical equipment or shaft openings. Converting it to co-working space triggers reclassification as an additional storey with cascading BHL, GFA, FAR, fire-rating, and egress consequences.

**If** a skylight uses corrugated wired glass with support mullions spaced 1.80 m apart…
**Then** this violates Sec. 1208.b — corrugated wired glass may span a maximum of **1.50 m** between supports. The 1.80 m span exceeds the maximum by 300 mm and requires either intermediate supports or a different glazing type.

**If** a rooftop tower has a cross-section of 12.00 sq.m measured at mid-height above the roof…
**Then** the supporting structural frame for that tower must extend all the way down to the **ground level** per Sec. 1210.e — the cross-section exceeds the 10.00 sq.m threshold that triggers the ground-frame requirement.

---

## Exam Traps

### Trap 1: The Two Penthouse Heights Are Not Interchangeable
A board question will describe a penthouse used as a generator room at 5.00 m above the roof and ask if it is code-compliant. Many candidates will recall the 8.40 m figure and answer "yes." The correct analysis: **8.40 m applies only to elevator machine rooms and tank enclosures** in non-Type V construction. A generator room is "other mechanical equipment" — it falls under the **3.60 m** limit. A generator room penthouse at 5.00 m above the roof violates Sec. 1210.a and is reclassified as an additional storey. Always identify the specific use before selecting the applicable height limit.

### Trap 2: The 1/3 Area Limit Is Aggregate, Not Per Structure
The exam may describe a building with three separate penthouse structures — an elevator room (80 sq.m), a water tank enclosure (60 sq.m), and a staircase bulkhead (70 sq.m) — on a roof of 600 sq.m, and ask if the largest single structure exceeds the limit. No individual structure exceeds 100 sq.m (which would be 1/6 of the roof), so each looks fine individually. But the **aggregate** is 210 sq.m, which equals **35% of 600 sq.m** — exceeding the 1/3 (200 sq.m) limit. Always sum all penthouse and roof structures for the aggregate check.

### Trap 3: Balcony Railings Must Be Incombustible Only Above 750 mm Grade — Not Below
Sec. 1209 requires incombustible railing materials for balconies, landings, and porches more than **750 mm above grade**. The exam may present a ground-floor patio with a 500 mm raised deck and ask what railing material is required — the answer is that Sec. 1209's incombustible requirement does not apply (the deck is below the 750 mm threshold), and any material permitted by the Type of Construction may be used. Do not apply the incombustible requirement to all railings universally — check the elevation first.

---

## Active Recall Questions

**Question 1**

A 20-storey condominium tower in Pasig City has a rooftop penthouse housing the elevator machine room. The supporting roof area measures 800 sq.m. The developer proposes a penthouse with a footprint of 220 sq.m and a height of 7.50 m above the roof deck. Evaluate the compliance of these dimensions under PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1210.

A. Both height and area are compliant — elevator rooms may rise 8.40 m and 220 sq.m is within 1/3 of 800 sq.m  
B. Height is compliant but area is non-compliant — 220 sq.m exceeds 1/3 of 800 sq.m (266.67 sq.m maximum)  
C. Area is compliant but height is non-compliant — 7.50 m exceeds the 3.60 m general limit  
D. Both are non-compliant — elevator rooms are limited to 3.60 m height and 1/4 of roof area  

> **Answer: A — Both dimensions are compliant**
>
> Under Sec. 1210.a, elevator machine room penthouses (in non-Type V construction) may rise up to **8.40 m** above the roof deck — the proposed 7.50 m is within this limit. Under Sec. 1210.b, aggregate penthouse area must not exceed **1/3 of the supporting roof area**: 1/3 × 800 sq.m = 266.67 sq.m. The proposed 220 sq.m is below this ceiling. Both dimensions comply. Option B misapplies the arithmetic — 220 sq.m < 266.67 sq.m, so area is compliant. Option C applies the 3.60 m limit incorrectly to an elevator room — 3.60 m applies only to "all other" penthouses, not elevator or tank enclosures. Option D is entirely incorrect on both limits.

---

**Question 2**

A heritage conservation architect is designing a skylight over a 3-storey library atrium in Intramuros. The proposed skylight uses flat wired glass panels. A structural engineer asks what the maximum allowable span between support mullions is per PD 1096. Concurrently, a corrugated wired glass alternative is proposed for wider bays. What are the correct maximum spans for both glass types?

A. Flat wired glass: 1.00 m; corrugated wired glass: 2.00 m  
B. Flat wired glass: 625 mm; corrugated wired glass: 1.50 m  
C. Flat wired glass: 500 mm; corrugated wired glass: 1.50 m  
D. Flat wired glass: 625 mm; corrugated wired glass: 1.20 m  

> **Answer: B — Flat: 625 mm; Corrugated: 1.50 m**
>
> Per Sec. 1208.b, flat wired glass skylights may span a maximum of **625 mm** between supports. Corrugated wired glass, benefiting from its structural ribbing, is permitted to span up to **1.50 m** between supports. These are hard maximum spans — exceeding them requires either additional support members or an alternative glazing system. Option A doubles both values incorrectly. Option C uses 500 mm for flat glass — below the actual 625 mm limit (not wrong from a safety standpoint but an incorrect code citation). Option D correctly identifies the flat glass span but reduces the corrugated span to 1.20 m, which is not the code figure.

---

**Question 3**

A property developer converts the mechanical penthouse of a completed 15-storey office building in Makati CBD into a private dining club. The penthouse occupies 28% of the roof area and rises 3.20 m above the roof deck. The zoning ordinance limits the building to 15 storeys and a Floor Area Ratio of 12.0. Which of the following best describes the primary regulatory consequence of this conversion under PD 1096?

A. The conversion is permitted provided the penthouse has proper fire exits, since 28% is within the 1/3 area limit and 3.20 m is within the 3.60 m height limit  
B. The conversion is non-compliant because 28% exceeds the 25% maximum penthouse coverage allowed under Sec. 1210  
C. The conversion causes the penthouse to be reclassified as an additional storey, potentially violating the 15-storey zoning limit and increasing the building's GFA toward the FAR ceiling  
D. The conversion is permitted as a change of use under Rule VII, Sec. 702, subject only to Building Official approval and issuance of a Certificate of Use  

> **Answer: C — Reclassification as an additional storey, triggering BHL and GFA/FAR violations**
>
> Per Sec. 1210.c, a penthouse may only be used to shelter mechanical equipment or vertical shaft openings. Converting it to a private dining club is a habitable use — expressly prohibited. The consequence is not merely a use violation: the penthouse is legally **treated as an additional storey**. This adds a 16th storey to a building permitted for only 15 storeys (violating the BHL zoning limit) and adds the penthouse floor area to the GFA computation (potentially pushing the building above the FAR = 12.0 ceiling). Option A is incorrect because the metric compliance (28% area, 3.20 m height) does not override the prohibited-use trigger — both conditions must be met. Option B invents a "25% maximum penthouse coverage" that does not exist in the Code (the limit is 1/3 = 33.3%). Option D is wrong because Rule VII governs change of occupancy for existing floors within the building — it cannot authorize the prohibited use of a penthouse, which remains governed by Sec. 1210.c regardless of any Certificate of Use.

---

<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule VII - Penthouses">


Per PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1210, penthouses have two height tiers: (1) elevator machine rooms and water tanks in non-Type V construction: max 8.40 m above roof; (2) all other penthouses: max 3.60 m above roof. Additionally, the aggregate area of all penthouses and roof structures must not exceed 1/3 of the supporting roof area. A penthouse used for any purpose other than sheltering mechanical equipment or shaft openings is reclassified as an additional storey — cascading into BHL, GFA, and FAR compliance issues.


</LawCallout>

<Warn >

The 8.40 m height limit applies ONLY to elevator machine rooms and water tank enclosures on non-Type V construction. A generator room penthouse at 5.00 m above the roof violates the 3.60 m general limit — not the 8.40 m limit. Always identify the specific penthouse use before selecting the applicable height tier.

</Warn>

<ExamTip >

On the LEA, expect a question that describes a penthouse with both dimensions and use, asking whether it complies. The correct analysis must check ALL three conditions simultaneously: (1) height within applicable tier, (2) aggregate area ≤1/3 of roof, (3) use is mechanical/shaft only. A single violation triggers reclassification.

</ExamTip>

## Spaced Repetition Reminder

**Session 1 (Today):** Memorize the two penthouse height limits (8.40 m and 3.60 m) and their specific applications. Write the fraction chain "1/3 roof — 1/4 frontage — 1/8 shaft" from memory. Read Exam Trap 1 carefully.

**Session 2 (Day 3):** Without looking at the article, draw a cross-section of a compliant penthouse with elevation dimensions and label all key requirements. Then check your sketch against the Cheat Sheet.

**Session 3 (Day 7):** Reconstruct the PH vs. USA comparison table entries for penthouse heights and skylight glazing. Explain the BHL exclusion logic — why does a prohibited-use penthouse trigger an additional storey classification?

**Session 4 (Day 14):** Work all three MCQs under timed conditions (90 seconds per question). Explain to a study partner why Option D in Question 3 is wrong. If you can articulate the Sec. 1210.c consequences without notes, this module is mastered.

*These articles are LEA board exam review materials based on PD 1096 (National Building Code of the Philippines) and cross-referenced with IBC provisions for comparative analysis. Always verify against the current edition of the implementing rules and regulations.*

---

## Cross‑References

**Ceiling Heights And Room Sizes**, **Allowable Floor Area Increases**, **Pd 1096 Rule Vii Height Limits**, **Exam Meta Deck Heights**

rows.content:
# Site Exterior Circulation

## Learning Goal

After reading this article, you should be able to:

Design site exterior circulation systems — driveways, walkways, loading areas, service access — under PD 1096 and BP 344: calculate minimum driveway width (3.00 m one-way, 6.00 m two-way) and turning radius by vehicle type; apply the 1.50 m minimum sidewalk width; and determine loading berth requirements by building use and gross floor area.
---
_Exterior Accessible Routes Integration Module – BP 344 + PD 1096 Context_[web:1][web:2][web:10][web:31][web:32][web:36][web:38][web:40][web:41][web:42]

---

## 1. Big Picture: From Street to Building

<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule VIII - Exterior Access">
BP 344 — The Accessibility Law mandates barrier-free access for PWDs in all public buildings.
</LawCallout>
Extracted summary:
- Props: (none)
- Text: BP 344 — The Accessibility Law mandates barrier-free access for PWDs in all p...

<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule VIII - Site Circulation">
BP 344 — The Accessibility Law mandates barrier-free access for PWDs in all public buildings.
</LawCallout>
Extracted summary:
- Props: (none)
- Text: BP 344 — The Accessibility Law mandates barrier-free access for PWDs in all p...

Goal: move a wheelchair user from **road → sidewalk → entrance → interior route** using only compliant slopes and widths under the updated BP 344 IRR, coordinated with PD 1096 site controls.[web:2][web:31][web:32]

Elements covered:

- Dropped sidewalks and curb ramps.
- Sidewalks, walkways, and pathways.
- Interface with PD 1096 lot lines, setbacks, PSO, and RROW (Rules VII & VIII).[web:35][web:38][web:40]

---

## 2. Dropped Sidewalks (BP 344 – Updated IRR)

Key requirements for dropped sidewalks at pedestrian crossings and ends of walkways:[web:2][web:10][web:31][web:33][web:42]

- Provide at **pedestrian crossings** and at ends of walkways of private streets/access roads.[web:2][web:33]
- Width: normally **corresponds to the width of the crossing** (e.g., 4.0 m minimum for national roads or as required by local ordinances for local roads).[web:33]
- For crossings/walkways **less than 1500 mm** wide:
  - Base/level surface at bottom of dropped sidewalk: minimum **1500‑mm depth**, width equal to the crossing/walkway width.[web:2][web:33]
- Maximum cross gradient: **1:100 (1%)**, sloped towards the road to avoid ponding.[web:2][web:33]
- Difference in elevation between base/level area and road/gutter: **≤ 19–25 mm** depending on specific diagram reference; most 2013–2024 materials show a small lip not exceeding around 19–25 mm.[web:2][web:33][web:42]
- Signage (where specified in updated IRR/tabs and local practice):
  - Pole‑mounted ISA sign, typically around **600 × 600 mm**, mounted with at least **2200 mm** headroom and located so it does not obstruct the path of travel.[web:31][web:32]
  - Pavement ISA sign at or near the center of the dropped sidewalk/curb ramp, sized proportionally to ramp width (often 600–800 mm as shown in reviewers).[web:31][web:32]

The **1500‑mm base pad** at the bottom is your primary **maneuvering area** at street level for turning and queueing.[web:2][web:33]

---

## 3. Curb Ramps at Drop‑Offs

For PWD drop‑off/loading bays (BP 344 IRR Appendix B – “Curb Ramps at Drop‑off Points”):[web:2][web:10][web:34][web:37][web:42]

- **Minimum width:** **900 mm**.[web:2][web:10][web:34][web:37]
- **Maximum gradient for the curb ramp run:** older IRR illustrations commonly show curb ramp runs not steeper than **1:12**, while some newer reviewer decks emphasize **1:15** as a conservative design slope; for exam purposes, keep **1:12** as the strict upper limit and treat 1:15 as a good‑practice gentler slope, especially over short rises.[web:1][web:2][web:34][web:42]
- Must not reduce the required sidewalk/walkway width or required level turn area: the curb ramp should be contained within or adjacent to the **minimum clear sidewalk/walkway width** and must preserve turning pads (see Section 4).[web:2][web:31][web:32]
- Use the same ISA wayfinding logic as dropped sidewalks: pole signage with adequate headroom and pavement markings aligned with the curb ramp.[web:31][web:32]

Think of curb ramps as **short, localized connectors** at the curb line; use full accessible ramps (with the wider minimum width and gentler slopes of the ramp section of BP 344) for larger level changes between street and entrance.[web:31][web:32][web:42]

---

## 4. Sidewalks, Walkways, and Pathways (Exterior “Corridors”)

Based on updated BP 344 IRR and 2024 reviewer summaries for pedestrian facilities:[web:2][web:31][web:32][web:36][web:41][web:42]

### 4.1 Width and Gradient

- **Minimum clear width:**
  - Older/official IRR: **1.20 m** minimum width for sidewalks/walkways.[web:1][web:2][web:42]
  - 2024 reviewer/amended IRR decks: often teach **1.50 m minimum** for main sidewalks, especially in high‑use public environments.[web:31][web:32][web:36]
  - For this module, treat **1.50 m as the exam‑oriented design minimum**, with the note that **1.20 m is the older absolute minimum** still cited in original IRR.
- Where two wheelchairs must pass: **1800 mm** width is recommended (and frequently cited in 2024 notes).[web:31][web:32]
- Longitudinal gradient: keep as level as practicable; **target not steeper than about 1:20 (5%)**, except where topography or site conditions necessitate ramps.[web:31][web:32]
- Cross gradient: maximum **1:100 (1%)**, to ensure drainage without discomfort.[web:1][web:2][web:42]

### 4.2 Continuity and Surface Quality

- Surfaces must be **slip‑resistant** in wet/dry conditions, continuous, and without abrupt changes in level greater than about **6 mm**; larger changes require bevels or ramps.[web:2][web:31][web:32]
- Gratings are discouraged along accessible paths; if unavoidable:[web:2][web:42]
  - Bars should be **perpendicular** to the direction of travel.
  - Maximum clear spacing around **13 mm** between bars.
  - Grating top surface should not be more than about **6 mm** above or below adjacent pavement.
  - Provide at least **30% luminance contrast** between grating and surrounding surface for visibility (per updated wayfinding/signage notes).[web:31][web:32]

### 4.3 Rest / Turn and Dead‑End Spaces

- In lengthy or busy sidewalks/walkways, provide places where a wheelchair can **turn around or pass another wheelchair**.[web:31][web:32]
- These **turnabout spaces** should be at least **1800 mm** in clear dimension (e.g., 1800 × 1800 mm squares).[web:31][web:32][web:36]
- Maximum spacing: about **12000 mm** between turnabout/rest spaces along long corridors or walkways.[web:31][web:32][web:36]
- Provide a turnabout/turning space at or within approximately **3500 mm** of every dead‑end corridor or exterior walkway dead‑end.[web:31][web:32]

Mnemonic (adjusted): **“1.2 code, 1.5 exam path, 1.8 pass, 12 m between, 3.5 m from dead‑end.”**

---

## 5. Tactile Paths and Warning Tiles Outside

From tactile floor surface provisions in updated IRR and wayfinding materials:[web:31][web:32][web:37][web:42]

- Tactile paths are required on primary pedestrian routes **within and approaching buildings**, typically linking public sidewalks, transport stops, entrances, counters, lifts, and toilets; recent reviewers commonly describe coverage within **several hundred meters** of major access points (e.g., transport stations to entrances), but check local IRR text for any fixed radius.[web:31][web:32][web:37]
- Use **directional tactile blocks** (parallel bars) along the route to guide visually impaired users to key destinations.[web:37][web:42]
- Use **warning tactile blocks** (domes) at hazards and decision points: stairs, ramps, escalator approaches, platform edges, major crossings, and gates.[web:37][web:42]
- Warning tactile strips typically:[web:31][web:32][web:37][web:42]
  - Have a depth of around **600 mm**.
  - Start approximately **300 mm** back from the actual hazard line (e.g., top/bottom of stairs, platform edge), so the user encounters the tactile cue before the drop.

This ties the **external tactile path** directly into interior tactile cues for stairs, elevators, and washrooms.

---

## 6. PD 1096 Context: Lot Lines, RROW, and Setbacks

From PD 1096 Rules VII & VIII summaries (classification, light & ventilation, PSO):[web:35][web:38][web:40]

- **Rule VII – Building Classification by Use or Occupancy:** affects occupancy group (residential, commercial, institutional, etc.), which in turn impacts required yards, courts, and allowable projections that your exterior accessible routes must respect.[web:15][web:35]
- **Rule VIII – Light and Ventilation / Percentage of Site Occupancy (PSO):**
  - Dictates **measurement of site occupancy** at ground level, exclusive of required courts, yards, and light wells.[web:35][web:38][web:40]
  - Specifies **maximum PSO** and minimum open space/court dimensions; sidewalks and accessible ramps inside the lot must sit within remaining open spaces without reducing courts and yards below minimum dimensions.[web:35][web:38][web:40]
- You cannot legally “solve accessibility” by over‑occupying open spaces or by permanently encroaching into the **public RROW** contrary to PD 1096, zoning, or local right‑of‑way ordinances; coordination with local road‑right‑of‑way standards is needed when aligning ramps and dropped sidewalks at the property line.[web:38][web:40]

Exam tip: when sketching site sections, show **property line, RROW, required front yard/court, sidewalk, ramp**, and building line all respecting PSO and court rules.

---

<ExamTip>**LEA Pattern:** Questions ask whether a building or space meets accessibility requirements. Calculate required number of accessible parking slots per total parking (1:100 ratio for first 500, then 1:200). Know the minimums.</ExamTip>

## 7. Active Recall – Site & Exterior Circulation

_(Updated to reflect both original IRR and 2024 reviewer practice values.)_

1. Minimum **code‑level** sidewalk/walkway width in the original BP 344 IRR? → **1200 mm**.[web:1][web:2]
2. Common **exam/reviewer** minimum sidewalk width used in 2024 notes? → **1500 mm**.[web:31][web:32][web:36]
3. Sidewalk/walkway width where two wheelchairs pass comfortably? → **1800 mm**.[web:31][web:32]
4. Maximum cross gradient for sidewalks/walkways? → **1:100 (1%)**.[web:1][web:2][web:42]
5. Minimum clear dimension for rest/turn (turnabout) spaces? → **1800 mm** (e.g., 1800 × 1800 mm).[web:31][web:32][web:36]
6. Maximum spacing between rest/turn spaces? → **12000 mm**.[web:31][web:32][web:36]
7. Distance from a dead‑end where a turnabout space must be provided? → within about **3500 mm** of the dead‑end.[web:31][web:32]
8. Minimum curb ramp width at PWD loading/drop‑off bays? → **900 mm**.[web:2][web:10][web:34][web:37]
9. Typical maximum curb ramp slope to remember? → **1:12** as strict upper limit, with **1:15** as a good‑practice gentler slope used in many 2024 reviewer materials.[web:1][web:2][web:34][web:42]

---

## Common Exam Traps

**TRAP 1 — Confusing sidewalk minimums:**
The original BP 344 IRR states **1.20 m** minimum sidewalk width. However, 2024 reviewer materials commonly teach **1.50 m** as the exam-oriented design minimum. Know both: 1.20 m is the code floor, 1.50 m is the exam/reviewer target. A question citing "original BP 344 IRR" expects 1.20 m.

**TRAP 2 — Curb ramp slope over 1:12:**
Curb ramp slopes steeper than **1:12** are non-compliant. The gentler **1:15** is a preferred design value, not the legal maximum. A curb ramp at 1:10 fails inspection.

**TRAP 3 — Missing rest/turn spaces:**
Rest/turn spaces of **1,800 mm** clear dimension must be provided **every 12,000 mm** along long walkways and **within 3,500 mm** of every dead-end. These are frequently omitted in site plans — and frequently tested.

**TRAP 4 — Grating orientation:**
Where gratings are unavoidable on accessible paths, bars must be **perpendicular** to travel direction with **≤ 13 mm** clear spacing. Parallel bars trap wheelchair casters and white canes.

**TRAP 5 — RROW encroachment:**
Accessible ramps, dropped sidewalks, and curb cuts inside the lot cannot permanently encroach on the public RROW or reduce required courts and yards below PD 1096 minimums. Coordinate with local road right-of-way standards.

---

<Note>
Common traps: confusing BP 344 with PD 1096, mixing up dimensions for ramps vs. stairs vs. handrails.

rows.title: Translating PWD Rights
rows.content:
# Translating PWD Rights
## Learning Goal

After reading this article, you should be able to:

Translate legal PWD rights (RA 7277, RA 9442, RA 10754, BP 344) into specific architectural design decisions: calculate the minimum number of accessible parking spaces (1 of 25, 2% of total), accessible toilet rooms, and accessible routes; identify the design requirements triggered by building occupancy, size, and type; and apply accessibility requirements to existing building alterations.
---
### The Complete Rights-to-Details Matrix for Philippine Licensure Examination for Architects

---

## REAL-WORLD HOOK

A CHED inspector walks through a newly completed state university campus in Mindanao. She is herself a wheelchair user. She checks the classrooms — the corridors are 1200 mm, just barely enough. The school toilet has no grab bar. The ramp to the library is 1:8 — too steep. The swimming pool has no transfer wall. The university president says proudly: "We complied with all the laws." The inspector opens her laptop and reads back to him: RA 7277 Section 12 (right to education), Section 23 (right to health), Section 30 (right to recreation). Then she asks a single question: *"Where, exactly in this campus, can a student in a wheelchair use any of these rights?"* This module maps every major PWD right in Philippine law to 2–3 concrete architectural details — so that you, the architect, are never the person who cannot answer that question.

---

## CORE MNEMONIC FRAMEWORK

### "**TIHERE-D**" — The Seven PWD Rights with Architectural Dimensions

| Letter | Right | Key Law Provision |
|--------|-------|-------------------|
| **T** | **Transport** — Right to Accessible Transport | RA 7277 Sec. 25 |
| **I** | **Information** — Right to Information & Communication | RA 7277 Sec. 29 |
| **H** | **Health** — Right to Health Services | RA 7277 Sec. 23 |
| **E** | **Education** — Right to Education | RA 7277 Sec. 12–14 |
| **R** | **Recreation & Culture** | RA 7277 Sec. 30 |
| **E** | **Employment** — Right to Work | RA 7277 Sec. 5–8 |
| **D** | **Discrimination** — Right Against Discrimination + Economic Rights | RA 9442 + RA 10754 |

> **Memory cue:** *"Every PWD has rights TIHERE-D — Transport, Information, Health, Education, Recreation, Employment, Discrimination-free."*

---

## THE MASTER RIGHTS-TO-DETAILS MATRIX

### RIGHT 1: Transport (RA 7277 Sec. 25)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to accessible public transport — including vehicles, terminals, stations, and pathways leading to and from transport facilities.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Level boarding platforms** | Floor height matches vehicle floor ±25 mm; platform edge marked with TGSI 300 mm back from edge | BP 344 + DPWH IRR |
| **Tactile paths at stations** | TGSI: directional bars (walking direction) 25 mm raised, 65 mm width; warning domes (hazard/turn) 5 mm raised; minimum strip width 300 mm | BP 344 Appendix A |
| **Ramp at terminal entry** | Slope ≤1:12, width ≥1200 mm, handrails at 700–900 mm both sides, landing 1500 mm at top and bottom | BP 344 |
| **Accessible parking at terminal** | Min stall: 4000 mm wide × 5000 mm long + 1800 mm access aisle; nearest to accessible entrance; ISA signage | BP 344 |
| **Elevator in multi-level transport facility** | Min cab: 1400 mm deep × 1500 mm wide, 900 mm door; Braille panel at 900–1200 mm AFF | BP 344 Sec. 5.6 |
| **Curb cuts / dropped sidewalk at station** | Flush with both sidewalk and road level; slope ≤1:12; detectable warning strip (TGSI domes) at top | BP 344 |
| **Accessible toilets at terminals** | Min 1800 × 2250 mm cubicle; 900 mm door; grab bars; accessible route from terminal concourse | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Queue management / waiting areas** | 5% of waiting seats designated PWD priority; accessible path to ticket counter; two-level counter | BP 344 Sec. 18.2.b.iii |

<Callout variant="lea-watch" title="Trap Leart">

"Level boarding" does NOT mean the platform is just paved. It means the platform edge height exactly (within ±25 mm) matches the vehicle floor height to eliminate the gap. A platform that requires a portable ramp is NOT level boarding.

</Callout>

---

### RIGHT 2: Information & Communication (RA 7277 Sec. 29)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to access information and communication in formats they can perceive and understand.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Visual/strobe alarms** | ≤3 flashes/sec (2–3 Hz); ≥2 candelas; white lens; word "FIRE" visible; placed in all rooms incl. bathrooms and bedrooms | BP 344 Sec. 17.8; NFPA 72 |
| **Braille signage on elevator jambs** | Grade 2 Braille; mounted at 1200 mm AFF on latch (opening) side of elevator door jamb | BP 344 |
| **Audio announcements / audio output** | ATMs, elevators, and public address systems must include audio guidance; ATMs must have audio output (headphone jack at min) | BP 344 Sec. 12.2 |
| **ISA signs** | UN Blue (Pantone 279); 600 × 600 mm on poles; mounted at 1800 mm to bottom; luminance contrast from background | BP 344 Appendix A |
| **General signage mounting height** | Max 1500 mm from floor to center of sign (for reach and visibility from wheelchair) | BP 344 |
| **Projecting signs** | Min 2200 mm vertical clearance below sign from floor | BP 344 |
| **Tactile maps at building entries** | Embossed floor plan with different textures for different spaces; Braille labels; 150 mm pictogram border; 50 mm tall letters; placed near main entrance | BP 344 |
| **Evacuation plans** | Embossed floor plans readable by blind and sighted; different textures per space type; located at each floor landing near stairwell | BP 344 |
| **Letter height by viewing distance** | ≤7 m → 60 mm; up to 50 m → 500 mm (see full table) | BP 344 Table A.7 |
| **Door signs** | Min 200 × 200 mm; on latch side; include Braille; at 1200–1500 mm AFF | BP 344 |
| **ATM kiosk signage** | Max 2400 mm AFF; Braille + tactile + audio output | BP 344 Sec. 12.2, 12.10 |
| **Frameless glass door marking** | Visual markers between 900 mm and 1500 mm AFF to prevent collision | BP 344 |

<Callout variant="lea-watch" title="faster flashing can trigger seizures in photosensitive persons. The exam may off">

The "≤3 flashes/sec" for strobe alarms refers to the maximum flash rate — faster flashing can trigger seizures in photosensitive persons. The exam may offer "5 flashes/sec" or "at least 3 flashes/sec" as distractors. Correct: no more than 3 flashes/sec.

</Callout>

---

### RIGHT 3: Health Services (RA 7277 Sec. 23)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to accessible health services, including facilities, equipment, and information.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Accessible hospital route from drop-off to ward** | Continuous accessible route: level or slope ≤1:20; min 1200 mm wide; no steps; all doors 900 mm clear; TGSI at intersections | BP 344 |
| **Accessible toilet/WC cubicle** | Min 1800 mm × 2250 mm (clear internal); 900 mm door swings out OR is sliding | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Grab bars — side of WC** | Horizontal bar on adjacent wall, 300 mm above WC seat height (typically 780 mm AFF for bar above 480 mm seat) | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Grab bars — rear of WC** | Horizontal bar on rear wall, at WC seat height + 300 mm | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Emergency call button (WC)** | 400–600 mm AFF (reachable from floor if person falls); activates audio/visual leart at nurses' station | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **WC seat height** | 450–480 mm AFF (standard accessible WC height) | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Lavatory (washbasin) under-clearance** | 650 mm high × 500 mm deep knee clearance; pipes insulated or covered | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Turning space in accessible toilet** | 1500 × 1500 mm clear floor space (not occupied by fixtures) | BP 344 Sec. 6 |
| **Hospital examination room** | Door 900 mm clear; 1500 × 1500 mm turning space inside; accessible examination table (adjustable height preferred) | BP 344 |
| **Accessible route to pharmacy counter** | Two-level counter: lower at 750 mm (wheelchair), higher at 950–1100 mm (standing); 1500 × 1500 mm approach space | BP 344 Sec. 14 |
| **Waiting area in clinic/hospital** | 5% of seating designated PWD priority; 900 × 1200 mm clear space beside each accessible seat; accessible path to all counters | BP 344 Sec. 18.2 |

---

### RIGHT 4: Education (RA 7277 Sec. 12–14)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to quality education — in mainstream schools, with support services, and in an accessible physical environment.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Accessible classroom corridors** | Min 1500 mm wide (school/education occupancy); clear height ≥2000 mm | BP 344 + PD 1096 |
| **Ramps at school buildings** | Required at all level changes; slope ≤1:12; width ≥1200 mm (1500 mm recommended in schools for two-way wheelchair traffic); handrails both sides | BP 344 |
| **Accessible toilet per floor** | At least one accessible toilet on each floor of each school building; min 1800 × 2250 mm; 900 mm door | BP 344 |
| **Classroom door** | Min 900 mm clear width; level threshold (max 12 mm); lever handle at 900 mm AFF | BP 344 |
| **Laboratory/workshop accessibility** | Accessible workstation at each type of lab (900 mm wide, 700 mm legroom, 480 mm depth); accessible route to all stations | BP 344 Sec. 15 |
| **Library accessible route** | Accessible path between all stacks (min 900 mm aisle); accessible study tables (750 mm height, 700 mm knee clearance); accessible toilet nearby | BP 344 |
| **Stage / presentation areas** | Accessible route to stage/podium; ramp if stage is elevated; min 900 mm width on stage access path | BP 344 |
| **Dormitory accessibility** | 2% of total rooms as accessible rooms (2024 IRR); lever handles; accessible toilet; visual alarms | BP 344 Sec. 17 (2024 IRR) |

<Callout variant="lea-watch" title="not "one per building" or "one per school." A 4-storey school must have an acces">

"Per floor" means each floor has an accessible toilet — not "one per building" or "one per school." A 4-storey school must have an accessible toilet on all 4 floors.

</Callout>

---

### RIGHT 5: Employment (RA 7277 Sec. 5–8)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to equal employment opportunity, reasonable accommodation, and accessible workplaces.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Accessible workstation** | Width ≥900 mm; knee clearance 700 mm high × 480 mm deep; 1500 × 1500 mm turning space at side | BP 344 Sec. 15 |
| **Accessible route in office** | Min 900 mm clear between workstations on primary path; min 1200 mm on main circulation corridors | BP 344 |
| **Office entrance** | Accessible from street/parking; dropped sidewalk; 900 mm door clear width; level threshold | BP 344 |
| **Break room / pantry** | Counter with knee clearance section at 750 mm (for wheelchair approach); accessible route to microwave/fridge controls ≤1200 mm AFF | BP 344 |
| **Accessible toilet** | At least one accessible toilet near work area; 1800 × 2250 mm minimum; 900 mm door | BP 344 |
| **Conference room** | Accessible table at 750 mm height; 700 mm knee clearance; min 1 accessible seat per 10 (no specific ratio, but at least 1 of each type under exercise equipment logic) | BP 344 |
| **Signage to accessible features** | ISA signage at main entrance; Braille + tactile on door signs; accessible toilet ISA sign | BP 344 |
| **Accessible parking** | Nearest to office entrance; 4000 mm stall + 1800 mm aisle; on flat or nearly flat grade | BP 344 |

---

### RIGHT 6: Recreation & Culture (RA 7277 Sec. 30)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to participate in cultural, artistic, recreational, and sporting activities.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Wheelchair seating in assembly/theater** | **3% of total seating** (2024 IRR); each space 900 mm × 1200 mm clear, firm, level; NOT in emergency egress path; access NOT through another wheelchair space | BP 344 2024 IRR Sec. 4 |
| **Wheelchair space access** | Each space served by accessible route; adjoins accessible circulation; companion seat adjacent (sports facilities) | BP 344 Sec. 4.3–4.4 |
| **Handrails at wheelchair seating** | 750 mm high at front and sides of wheelchair space | BP 344 Sec. 4.7 |
| **Swimming pool — transfer wall** | Height: **450 mm**; transfer space: 1500 × 1500 mm beside transfer wall; slope ≤1:12 approaching | BP 344 Sec. 1 |
| **Exercise equipment** | At least **one of each type** provided with: 900 × 1200 mm clear floor space; served by accessible route | BP 344 Sec. 3.4.a |
| **Sports facility companion seat** | Must be adjacent to wheelchair spaces; same sightlines as wheelchair user | BP 344 Sec. 3.3.a |
| **Museum / gallery accessible route** | Min 1200 mm between exhibit cases; exhibits at reachable height (750–1200 mm AFF for key information); accessible path to all gallery areas | BP 344 |
| **Accessible Balechers/grandstands** | Accessible route to all sections; ramps or lifts where level changes; handrails at all ramps and stairs | BP 344 |
| **Spectator restrooms** | At least one accessible WC per gender per facility level; 1800 × 2250 mm cubicle | BP 344 Sec. 6 |

<Callout variant="lea-watch" title="50 seats → 2 spaces; 51–300 → 4; 301–500 → 6) was">

The old tiered table (4–50 seats → 2 spaces; 51–300 → 4; 301–500 → 6) was replaced in the 2024 IRR by the flat 3% rule. The old table may still appear in exams — know BOTH. If the question says "2024 IRR" or "current standard," use 3%. If it says "old IRR" or gives numbers matching the old table, use the old table.

</Callout>

---

### RIGHT 7: Right Against Discrimination & Economic Rights (RA 9442 + RA 10754)

> **Legal Text:** PWDs have the right to be free from discrimination, ridicule, and exclusion. They have the right to 20% discount + 12% VAT exemption on covered goods and services.

| Architectural Feature | Specification | Standard |
|----------------------|---------------|----------|
| **Priority counter / express lane** | Required in all government offices, hospitals, banks, pharmacies, commercial establishments; must have ISA signage | RA 9442 + BP 344 |
| **Two-level service counter** | Lower level: **750 mm** (wheelchair user); Higher level: **950–1100 mm** (standing user); min counter width: 900 mm; 700 mm knee clearance at lower level | BP 344 Sec. 14 |
| **Approach space at counter** | 1500 × 1500 mm clear floor on patron side; 1500 × 1500 mm on service side | BP 344 Sec. 14.4 |
| **Accessible pharmacy/drugstore** | Accessible route from entrance to dispensing counter; counter at 750 mm lower level; accessible toilet nearby | BP 344 + RA 10754 |
| **Accessible restaurant counter** | Same two-level design (750/950–1100 mm); 10% of dining tables at 750 mm height with 700 mm knee clearance | BP 344 Sec. 16 |
| **Queue barrier design** | Barriers (stanchions/ropes) must allow 900 mm clear width for wheelchair entry; accessible bypass lane if standard queues are narrow | BP 344 |
| **ATM accessibility** | Controls at 900–1200 mm AFF; Braille + tactile + audio output; 1800 × 1800 mm clear space in front; counter at 750 mm | BP 344 Sec. 12 |
| **Hotel accessible rooms** | 2% of total guest rooms (2024 IRR); lever handles; dual peepholes (lower at 1000 mm); visual strobe alarms; vibrating pillow alarm; accessible toilet; bed max 500 mm height | BP 344 Sec. 17 |
| **Accessible hospital admission counter** | Two-level: 750 mm / 950–1100 mm; ISA signage; 1500 × 1500 mm approach space | BP 344 Sec. 14 |

---

## COMPREHENSIVE RIGHTS-TO-DETAILS SUMMARY TABLE

| Right | Law | Key Detail 1 | Key Detail 2 | Key Detail 3 |
|-------|-----|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| Transport | RA 7277 Sec. 25 | Level boarding ±25 mm | TGSI at platform edges | Accessible parking 4000 × 5000 mm + 1800 mm aisle |
| Information | RA 7277 Sec. 29 | Strobe alarm ≤3 flashes/sec | Braille at 1200 mm on elevator jamb | Audio output on ATMs |
| Health | RA 7277 Sec. 23 | WC 1800 × 2250 mm | Grab bar 300 mm above WC seat | Emergency call button 400–600 mm AFF |
| Education | RA 7277 Sec. 12–14 | Corridors 1500 mm in schools | Accessible toilet per floor | Ramp slope ≤1:12 |
| Employment | RA 7277 Sec. 5–8 | Workstation 900 mm wide, 700 mm knee clearance | Accessible route 900 mm min | Accessible parking nearest entry |
| Recreation | RA 7277 Sec. 30 | 3% wheelchair seating (2024 IRR) | Pool transfer wall 450 mm | 1 of each exercise type accessible |
| Anti-discrimination | RA 9442 | Priority counter (ISA sign) | Two-level counter 750/950–1100 mm | Express lane in all covered establishments |
| Economic (discount) | RA 10754 | Accessible pharmacy counter | Accessible hospital counter | 20% discount + 12% VAT exempt requires accessible access to claim it |

---

## SECTION: DETAILS DEEP DIVE

### The Accessible Toilet Cubicle — Full Specification

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           ACCESSIBLE WC CUBICLE                     │
│           Min 1800 mm × 2250 mm (clear)             │
│                                                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────┐   ▲                        │
│  │                     │   │                        │
│  │   1500 × 1500 mm    │   │ TURNING                │
│  │   TURNING SPACE     │   │ RADIUS                 │
│  │   (clear floor)     │   │                        │
│  │                     │   ▼                        │
│  └──────────┬──────────┘                            │
│             │                                       │
│    ┌────────┴──────────────────────────────┐        │
│    │  GRAB BAR — side wall                 │ ←900mm │
│    │  (300 mm above WC seat AFF)           │ AFF    │
│    │  ──────────────────────────────       │        │
│    │                                       │        │
│    │  [WC]  ←seat at 450–480 mm AFF        │        │
│    │                                       │        │
│    │  GRAB BAR — rear wall                 │        │
│    └───────────────────────────────────────┘        │
│                                                     │
│   EMERGENCY CALL BUTTON: 400–600 mm AFF             │
│   (reachable from floor if person falls)            │
│                                                     │
│   DOOR: 900 mm clear, swings OUT or slides          │
│   Lever handle at 900 mm AFF                        │
│   Threshold: max 12 mm                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The Two-Level Service Counter — Full Specification

```
   Standing user height: 1600–1800 mm
   Seated (wheelchair) user height: 1150–1350 mm

   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │    HIGHER LEVEL: 950–1100 mm AFF             │ ← for standing users
   │    ──────────────────────────────────────    │
   │                                              │
   │    LOWER LEVEL: 750 mm AFF                   │ ← for wheelchair users
   │    [KNEE CLEARANCE: 700 mm high × 480 mm deep]   
   │    ──────────────────────────────────────    │
   │                                              │
   │    COUNTER WIDTH: min 900 mm                 │
   │                                              │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

         APPROACH SPACE: 1500 × 1500 mm (patron side)
```

### Wheelchair Seating in Assembly — 3% Rule Application

| Total Seats | 3% (rounded up) | Old IRR equivalent |
|------------|----------------|-------------------|
| 100 | 3 spaces | 4 (51–300 → 4) |
| 200 | 6 spaces | 4 (51–300 → 4) |
| 300 | 9 spaces | 4 (51–300 → 4) |
| 400 | 12 spaces | 6 (301–500 → 6) |
| 500 | 15 spaces | 6 (301–500 → 6) |
| 1000 | 30 spaces | 11 (6 + 5 extra per 100) |
| 2000 | 60 spaces | 21 (6 + 15 extra per 100) |

> **Observation:** For smaller venues (100–300 seats), the **2024 IRR 3% rule requires fewer spaces** than the old tiered table. For mid-size (500 seats), they are roughly equivalent. For large venues (1000+), the **3% rule requires more spaces**. Know both — the exam tests both.

---

## 10 Q&A DRILL: RIGHTS TO DESIGNS

**Q1.** A subway station is being designed. What architectural feature translates the Right to Transport (RA 7277 Sec. 25) into a physical element at the platform edge?

<Warn>

A: A level boarding platform — the platform floor height must match the vehicle (train/bus) floor height within ±25 mm, eliminating the vertical gap. TGSI warning domes must be installed 300 mm back from the platform edge to provide a tactile safety warning.

</Warn>

---

**Q2.** A deaf PWD checks into a hotel. Under the Right to Information (RA 7277 Sec. 29), what two room features must be present?

> **A:**
> 1. **Visual/strobe alarm** — max 3 flashes/sec, min 2 candelas, white lens, word "FIRE" visible — in all rooms including bathrooms (BP 344 Sec. 17.8)
> 2. **Vibrating pillow or bed alarm** — to leart deaf or hard-of-hearing guests to emergencies (BP 344 Sec. 17.10)

---

**Q3.** A 1800 × 2250 mm accessible WC cubicle is designed. The grab bar is on the side wall. What is the correct height of the grab bar above the floor?

> **A:** The grab bar should be **300 mm above the WC seat height**. With a standard accessible WC seat at 450–480 mm AFF, the grab bar is approximately **750–780 mm AFF**. The measurement is from the WC seat, not from the floor independently.

---

**Q4.** A private university claims it does not need accessible toilets on every floor because "the elevator goes to all floors." Is this correct under the Right to Education?

<LawCallout code="bp344" section="Section 2 - PWD Rights">


A: No. BP 344 requires at least one accessible toilet on each floor served by the building — the elevator provides access to the floor, but the accessible toilet must be on that floor. A PWD should not have to go to a different floor to use an accessible toilet.


</LawCallout>

---

**Q5.** An office renovation for a company with 200 employees. Under the Right to Employment (RA 7277 Sec. 5–8), what are the minimum workstation dimensions for a wheelchair user?

> **A:** **Width: 900 mm; Knee clearance: 700 mm high × 480 mm deep**. A turning space of 1500 × 1500 mm must be available beside the workstation. The workstation must be served by an accessible route of at least 900 mm clear width.

---

**Q6.** A new 2000-seat cinema is being designed. How many wheelchair spaces are required under the 2024 IRR, and what are the dimensions of each space?

> **A:** **3% × 2000 = 60 wheelchair spaces.** Each space must be: **900 mm wide × 1200 mm deep** (front/rear entry), on a clear, firm, level surface. Access to each space must not pass through another wheelchair space.

---

**Q7.** Under RA 9442 (Right Against Discrimination), a bank must provide a priority counter. What are the exact height dimensions of this two-level counter?

> **A:** Lower level (for wheelchair users): **750 mm AFF.** Higher level (for standing users): **950–1100 mm AFF.** Minimum counter width: **900 mm.** Knee clearance at lower level: **700 mm high × 480 mm deep.**

---

**Q8.** A swimming pool complex is being renovated. Under the Right to Recreation (RA 7277 Sec. 30), what physical feature must be added to the pool to make it accessible for wheelchair users who cannot swim independently?

> **A:** A **transfer wall at 450 mm AFF** — a raised ledge at the pool edge that allows a wheelchair user to transfer from their chair to the pool edge and slide in. A **1500 × 1500 mm transfer space** (slope ≤1:12) must adjoin the transfer wall.

---

**Q9.** Under RA 10754 (20% discount + 12% VAT exemption), a PWD goes to a pharmacy. The dispensing counter is 900 mm high with no knee clearance. What architectural deficiency is this, and which specific dimension must be corrected?

> **A:** The counter has no accessible section. The pharmacy must provide a **lower counter level at 750 mm AFF** with **700 mm knee clearance** underneath (and 480 mm depth) so a wheelchair user can approach and claim their discount. The right to the discount is meaningless without accessible physical access to the counter.

---

**Q10.** An emergency call button in an accessible hospital toilet is mounted at 1200 mm AFF. Is this compliant?

> **A:** **No.** The emergency call button must be at **400–600 mm AFF** — low enough to be reached by a person who has fallen to the floor. At 1200 mm, a fallen person cannot reach it. This is a life-safety failure, not just a technical noncompliance.

---

## REASON FOR THE LAW

> **Why does every right need a physical translation?**
>
<LawCallout code="bp344" section="Section 3 - Scope">


Rights written in law are abstractions until they are expressed in stone, concrete, and steel. RA 7277 grants PWDs the right to education — but a school with no ramps and narrow corridors makes that right a legal fiction. RA 10754 gives PWDs a 20% discount — but a pharmacy counter at 900 mm with no knee clearance denies a wheelchair user the ability to stand at that counter long enough to claim it. The architect is the translator: the person who converts abstract rights into millimeter dimensions, slope ratios, and grab bar locations. When you understand that each detail in BP 344 is a physical embodiment of a constitutional right, you stop treating accessibility as a compliance checklist and start treating it as the craft of justice.


</LawCallout>

---

## TRAP LEARTS (MASTER LIST)

> **🚨 TRAP 1 — Grab Bar Height**
> The grab bar is 300 mm **above the WC seat**, not 300 mm above the floor. With the seat at 450–480 mm, the bar is ~750–780 mm AFF. Distractors often say "300 mm AFF" or "900 mm AFF."

> **🚨 TRAP 2 — Emergency Call Button Height**
> Call button = **400–600 mm AFF** (low, reachable from floor). Do NOT confuse with light switches (1200 mm AFF) or electrical outlets (450 mm min AFF).

> **🚨 TRAP 3 — 3% vs Old Wheelchair Seating Table**
> 2024 IRR = 3% flat rate. Old IRR = tiered (4-50→2, etc.). Both may appear. The question context tells you which to use. If no date context given, use the 2024 IRR (3%).

> **🚨 TRAP 4 — Pool Transfer Wall Height**
> Transfer wall = **450 mm** AFF. This is not a ramp height, not a grab bar height, not a bench height. It is specific to pool transfer walls only.

> **🚨 TRAP 5 — "One Accessible Room per Building" vs 2%**
> The old IRR provided "1 per 50 rooms." The 2024 IRR mandates **2% of total guest rooms** as accessible. Government-owned accommodation: **10%**. Know all three.

> **🚨 TRAP 6 — Two-Level Counter Heights**
> Lower: **750 mm** (always). Higher: **950–1100 mm** (range). The exam may test "what is the higher level height?" — the answer is a range, not a single number. Any value between 950 and 1100 mm is correct.

> **🚨 TRAP 7 — Strobe Flash Rate**
> Maximum **3 flashes per second** (not "at least 3"). More than 3 flashes/sec can cause seizures in photosensitive PWDs. The limit is a MAXIMUM, not a minimum.

---

## ACTIVE RECALL DRILL

**Q1.** What right does RA 7277 Sec. 25 protect, and name one specific architectural dimension it requires.
> **A:** Right to Accessible Transport. One detail: accessible parking stall **4000 mm wide + 1800 mm access aisle**.

**Q2.** What is the minimum dimension of an accessible WC cubicle?
> **A:** **1800 mm × 2250 mm** (clear interior dimensions).

**Q3.** At what height is the emergency call button in an accessible toilet?
> **A:** **400–600 mm AFF** (reachable from the floor if the user falls).

**Q4.** How many wheelchair spaces are required in a 500-seat theater under the 2024 IRR?
> **A:** 3% × 500 = **15 spaces**.

**Q5.** What are the two heights of a two-level service counter?
> **A:** Lower: **750 mm**; Upper: **950–1100 mm**.

**Q6.** What is the height of the transfer wall at an accessible swimming pool?
> **A:** **450 mm AFF**.

**Q7.** Under RA 10754, what percentage discount do PWDs receive on medicine?
> **A:** **20% discount + 12% VAT exemption**.

**Q8.** What is the maximum flash rate for a visual fire alarm strobe in a hotel room?
> **A:** **≤3 flashes/sec** (not more than 3 Hz).

---

## PROTÉGÉ EFFECT CHALLENGE

> **Your task:** A city councilor asks you to testify at a hearing on accessibility compliance in local hospitals. Using only what you know from this module, prepare a 5-point testimony covering:
>
> 1. Which right in RA 7277 covers hospital accessibility, and what it means in physical terms
> 2. The exact dimensions of the accessible WC cubicle every hospital must provide
> 3. Why the emergency call button placement is a life-safety issue, not just a design detail
> 4. What a two-level counter means and why every pharmacy, including hospital pharmacies, needs one
> 5. How RA 10754's 20% discount cannot be physically claimed without proper counter design
>
> If you can testify fluently on all five points without notes, you understand how law becomes architecture. If any point is unclear, return to its section.

---

*Module 10 | From Law to Detail — Translating PWD Rights | Philippine LEA Review Series*

---



---

## Exam Tip

LEA Trap: Key design translations from PWD laws: RA 7277 = accessible parking (1 per 25 slots min), accessible toilets (1 per floor), ramps | RA 9442 = 20% discount (triggers NO design change, it is an economic privilege) | BP 344 = specific dimensional requirements (tactile warnings, counter heights, grab bars). The most tested: RA 7277 mandates facilities, RA 9442 mandates discounts — DO NOT confuse them.

## Cross‑References

**Law Qa Deck Ra 7277 9442 10754**, **Ra 9442 Pwd Privileges And Incentives**, **Accessible Seating In Assembly Areas**, **Wheelchair Maneuvering And Parking**
